basis: Congenital joint rigidity defines a musculoskeletal disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Acanthamoeba infection directly damages the cornea; associated ocular complications remain within the ocular axis.
Bacterial infection umbrella spanning neurologic, soft-tissue and other presentations; no anatomical organ applies across most forms.
Developmental disability, skin abnormalities and cardiac disease are defining; skeletal abnormalities/joint laxity occur in 30-99%. Ocular and dental defects omitted by cap.
Respiratory-chain disorder; leukodystrophy/cognitive decline 2/2, muscle weakness with abnormal fibers 2/2, cardiomyopathy 1/1 assessed. Small series; visual loss may be cerebral.
Manganese transport disorder; neurotoxic accumulation with dystonia characterizes both listed forms. Liver disease and polycythemia are subtype-dependent.
Glucagon receptor dysfunction causes endocrine pancreatic alpha-cell hyperplasia and tumors. Pancreatitis and gallstones are separately diagnosed conditions.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy directly affects erythrocytes and spleen. Retinopathy and osteonecrosis are separately diagnosed complications; other organ injuries lack a clear 30% rate.
Patent ductus arteriosus is a congenital cardiovascular malformation.
Organism-defined bacterial infection; skin, respiratory and systemic presentations vary, with no anatomical site specified for the umbrella.
Inflammation affects periarticular tissues. Inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
Dental root and pulp-chamber dysplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Renal lesions in 80-99%; cardiac rhabdomyomas in 30-79% and a major criterion. Retinal hamartomas omitted by cap; pulmonary LAM is separately diagnosed.
Carcinoma originates in breast tissue, which has no axis; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ labels.
Calculus is located within the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urethral or bladder damage is not established.
Enamel defects, gingival fibromatosis and nephrocalcinosis define this enamel-renal syndrome; renal dysfunction is also frequent.
Melanocytic neoplasm arises in the leptomeninges; its CNS origin determines the axis.
Intellectual disability defines the disease; structural foot deformity occurs in 7/11 and hearing impairment in 4/9. Deep-set eyes alone do not establish ocular damage.
Adrenal steroidogenesis defect with hypogonadism and hypokalemia; severe hypertension is defining and occurs in 80-99%.
Eye malformations, osteopetrosis and congenital deafness define COMMAD. Albinism is also defining, with generalized hypopigmentation in 1/2 reported patients.
Hepatic glycogen metabolism disorder with hepatomegaly and frequent fibrosis. Muscle and neurodevelopmental injury are occasional, below 30%.
RAG1 deficiency disrupts adaptive immune development and causes severe combined immunodeficiency; secondary infections are separate diseases.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; the translocation does not establish common damage to another organ.
Sulfur mustard characteristically causes chemical injury to skin, eyes and respiratory epithelium. Marrow suppression occurs mainly with severe systemic exposure.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with epilepsy and ragged-red fibers; sensorineural hearing loss in 80-99%. Optic atrophy and lipomas in 30-79% omitted by cap.
